q: The original grant for a work is Rs 840 lakh. A supplementary grant of Rs 75 lakh is obtained during the year, and Rs 40 lakh is surrendered from the work. The final grant of the work is:

options.A: Rs 800 lakh
options.B: Rs 915 lakh
options.C: Rs 955 lakh
options.D: Rs 875 lakh

e: Final grant = original grant + supplementary grant - amount surrendered = 840 + 75 - 40 = Rs 875 lakh.

q: A road over-bridge costing Rs 26,00,000 is constructed in lieu of a level crossing on a cost-sharing basis, the cost being shared equally between the Railways and the State Government. The share of the State Government is:
e: The cost is shared equally between the Railways and the State Government, so the State's share = 26,00,000 / 2 = Rs 13,00,000.

q: A deposit work is executed by the Railways at a cost of Rs 40,00,000. Departmental charges are leviable on the work at 12.5 per cent of the cost. The total amount recoverable from the party on whose behalf the work is executed is:
e: Departmental charges = 12.5/100 x 40,00,000 = Rs 5,00,000; total recoverable from the party = 40,00,000 + 5,00,000 = Rs 45,00,000.

q: A railway project involves a capital investment of Rs 150 crore. Its anticipated gross earnings are Rs 40 crore per annum and the anticipated working expenses are Rs 22 crore per annum. The anticipated rate of return on the capital invested is:

options.A: 8 per cent
options.B: 12 per cent
options.C: 15 per cent
options.D: 26.7 per cent

e: Net gain = gross earnings - working expenses = 40 - 22 = Rs 18 crore; rate of return = 18/150 x 100 = 12 per cent.

q: Earthwork in an embankment is executed over a length of 200 metres, with an average cross-sectional area of 12 square metres. The quantity of earthwork executed is:

options.A: 2,000 cubic metres
options.B: 212 cubic metres
options.C: 1,200 cubic metres
options.D: 2,400 cubic metres

e: Quantity of earthwork = length x average cross-sectional area = 200 x 12 = 2,400 cubic metres.

q: The rate of dividend payable by the Railways to the general revenues on their capital-at-charge is determined on the basis of the recommendations of:

options.A: The Finance Commission of India
options.B: The Railway Convention Committee, as adopted by Parliament
options.C: The NITI Aayog
options.D: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India

e: The rate of dividend payable by the Railways on their capital-at-charge is determined on the basis of the recommendations of the Railway Convention Committee, as adopted by Parliament.

q: Under the Public Procurement Policy for Micro and Small Enterprises, every Central Ministry, Department and public sector undertaking is required to achieve a minimum annual procurement target from micro and small enterprises of:

options.A: 10 per cent of its total annual procurement
options.B: 15 per cent of its total annual procurement
options.C: 20 per cent of its total annual procurement
options.D: 25 per cent of its total annual procurement

e: Under the Public Procurement Policy for Micro and Small Enterprises, every Central Ministry, Department and PSU must achieve a minimum annual procurement target of 25 per cent of its total annual procurement from MSEs.

q: Under the Public Procurement (Preference to Make in India) Order, where the lowest bidder is not a Class-I local supplier, a Class-I local supplier is given an opportunity to match the lowest price if his quoted price is within the margin of purchase preference. The margin of purchase preference is:

options.A: 10 per cent
options.B: 15 per cent
options.C: 20 per cent
options.D: 25 per cent

e: Under the Make in India order, the margin of purchase preference is 20 per cent: a Class-I local supplier within that margin of the lowest bid gets the opportunity to match the lowest price.

q: Under the 'Bid Security Declaration' introduced in Government procurement in lieu of earnest money deposit, the bidder signs a declaration accepting that:

options.A: He will be suspended from participating in the tender process for the period specified in the bid documents if he withdraws or modifies his bid during its validity, or fails to execute the contract or furnish performance security after its award
options.B: His security deposit under all other contracts with the Railways will be forfeited if he withdraws his bid
options.C: He will pay a penalty equal to twice the earnest money if his tender is not accepted
options.D: His bid will be treated as the lowest bid for the work

e: Under a Bid Security Declaration, the bidder accepts that he will be suspended from the tender process for the period specified in the bid documents if he withdraws or modifies his bid during validity, or fails to execute the contract or furnish performance security after award.

q: Tax is not required to be deducted at source under Section 194C of the Income-tax Act in respect of a single payment made to a contractor where the amount of such payment does not exceed:
e: Under Section 194C, no TDS is required on a single payment to a contractor where the amount does not exceed Rs 30,000.

q: A tenderer communicates his acceptance of the Letter of Acceptance subject to conditions which are at variance with the conditions of the tender. In law, such an acceptance:

options.A: Concludes the contract on the tenderer's conditions
options.B: Concludes the contract on the tender conditions, the extra conditions being ignored
options.C: Extends the validity of the tender automatically
options.D: Amounts to a counter-offer, and no contract is concluded unless the Railways accept those conditions

e: Acceptance of the Letter of Acceptance subject to conditions at variance with the tender conditions is not a valid acceptance; in law it amounts to a counter-offer, and no contract is concluded unless the Railways accept those conditions.

q: Where a works contract does not name any sum as liquidated damages, a party claiming ordinary (unliquidated) damages for breach of the contract is required to:

options.A: Prove the actual loss suffered by him on account of the breach
options.B: Claim any amount, whether or not any loss has been suffered
options.C: Claim a fixed percentage of the contract value in all cases
options.D: Obtain the sanction of the Railway Board before claiming damages

e: Where the contract names no liquidated damages, a party claiming ordinary (unliquidated) damages must prove the actual loss suffered on account of the breach; damages are not payable as a matter of course.

q: An order banning business dealings with a firm, issued by a zonal railway, is applicable:

options.A: On all the Railways of India automatically
options.B: Only to the production units of the Railways
options.C: Only within that zonal railway, unless the Railway Board issues or endorses the order for application all over the Indian Railways
options.D: Only to the division which issued the order

e: A banning order issued by a zonal railway applies only within that railway, unless the Railway Board issues or endorses it for application all over the Indian Railways.

q: Although a bank guarantee is an independent undertaking of the bank, a court will ordinarily restrain its invocation by the Railways only in exceptional circumstances, such as:

options.A: A request made by the contractor on grounds of hardship
options.B: Established fraud in connection with the guarantee, or irretrievable injustice if the invocation is allowed
options.C: The pendency of arbitration proceedings between the parties
options.D: The contractor having offered alternative security

e: A bank guarantee is an independent undertaking, so courts restrain its invocation only in exceptional circumstances such as established fraud or irretrievable injustice if the invocation is allowed to proceed.

q: The price charged to a tenderer for the tender documents of a work is:

options.A: Not refundable, whether or not his tender is accepted
options.B: Refunded to all tenderers after the tender is decided
options.C: Adjusted against the earnest money of every tenderer
options.D: Refunded only to the successful tenderer

e: The price charged for tender documents is not refundable, whether or not the tenderer's bid is accepted, as it is the cost of the documents supplied to him.

q: In e-tendering through IREPS, a tenderer who has submitted his bid may withdraw or modify the bid:

options.A: At any time before the work is awarded
options.B: Only after the tenders are opened
options.C: Only with the permission of the Tender Committee
options.D: At any time before the due date and time fixed for submission of bids

e: In e-tendering through IREPS, a tenderer may withdraw or modify his submitted bid at any time before the due date and time fixed for submission of bids; thereafter the bid is frozen.

q: In a works contract, the amount of work done against the labour component is Rs 20,00,000. The cost index for labour rises from 250 at the time of tendering to 280 for the period of the bill. The price variation payable on the labour component is:
e: Price variation on the labour component = amount of work done x (new index - old index) / old index = 20,00,000 x (280 - 250)/250 = 20,00,000 x 30/250 = Rs 2,40,000.

q: A contractor who has not furnished his Permanent Account Number (PAN) is paid Rs 5,00,000 for a works contract. The tax deductible at source under Section 206AA of the Income-tax Act, at the higher rate of 20 per cent, amounts to:
e: Under Section 206AA, tax is deducted at 20 per cent where the payee has not furnished his PAN: 20/100 x 5,00,000 = Rs 1,00,000.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The setting time of cement is determined by means of the Vicat apparatus.
2. The soundness of cement is tested by means of the Le Chatelier apparatus.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: the setting time of cement is determined with the Vicat apparatus, and its soundness is tested with the Le Chatelier apparatus.

q: Rails in a track are not laid vertically, but are tilted inwards at a slope of 1 in 20, primarily in order to:

options.A: Bring the head of the rail in proper bearing with the coned tread of the wheels
options.B: Reduce the gauge of the track on curves
options.C: Prevent the creep of rails in the track
options.D: Facilitate the welding of rail joints

e: Rails are tilted inwards at 1 in 20 to match the coning of the wheel treads, so that the rail head bears properly with the coned tread of the wheels and the load is transmitted centrally.

q: The two rail sections now standardised for use on broad gauge main lines of the Indian Railways are:

options.A: 44.7 kg per metre and 52 kg per metre
options.B: 52 kg per metre and 90 kg per metre
options.C: 60 kg per metre and 75 kg per metre
options.D: 52 kg per metre and 60 kg per metre

e: The two rail sections now standardised for broad gauge main lines are 52 kg per metre and 60 kg per metre, the heavier section being used for heavier and faster traffic.

q: In jointed track, a small gap is deliberately left between the ends of two adjoining rails at a rail joint in order to:

options.A: Reduce the noise produced by passing trains
options.B: Allow for the expansion of the rails with a rise in temperature
options.C: Permit drainage of water from the track
options.D: Facilitate the replacement of fish plates

e: A small expansion gap is left between adjoining rail ends in jointed track to allow the rails to expand with a rise in temperature, preventing buckling of the track.

q: The crossing (frog) provided in a turnout serves the purpose of:

options.A: Enabling the flange of a wheel travelling on one rail to cross the other rail at the place where the two rails intersect
options.B: Locking the tongue rails in position after the points are set
options.C: Connecting the two tongue rails so that they move together
options.D: Supporting the rails at the heel of the switch

e: The crossing (frog) enables the flange of a wheel travelling on one rail to pass across the other rail at the point where the two rails intersect in a turnout.

q: Trap points are provided at the exit of a siding or a yard line where it joins a running line in order to:

options.A: Speed up the movement of trains leaving the siding
options.B: Measure the speed of vehicles entering the running line
options.C: Derail any vehicle which moves out of the siding without authority, before it can foul the running line
options.D: Hold the wagons placed in the siding against rolling

e: Trap points at the exit of a siding derail any vehicle which moves out without authority, before it can foul the running line and endanger trains on it.

q: A 'scissor crossover' between two parallel tracks consists of:

options.A: A single crossover with a diamond crossing in its middle
options.B: Two crossovers crossing each other, so that trains can cross from either track to the other in both directions
options.C: Two turnouts laid back to back on the same track
options.D: A crossover provided exclusively for shunting movements

e: A scissor crossover consists of two crossovers crossing each other between two parallel tracks, with a diamond crossing in the middle, so trains can cross from either track to the other in both directions.

q: On sharp curves, the gauge of the track is widened slightly in order to:

options.A: Increase the cant that can be provided on the curve
options.B: Reduce the speed of trains on the curve
options.C: Prevent the derailment of trains due to excessive flange pressure
options.D: Permit the easy passage of the rigid wheel base of bogies through the curve and reduce wear of the rails and wheel flanges

e: On sharp curves the gauge is widened slightly to permit the easy passage of the rigid wheel base of bogies through the curve and to reduce wear of the rails and wheel flanges.

q: A level crossing is said to be 'interlocked' when:

options.A: Its gates or barriers are interlocked with the signals, so that the signal for a train cannot be cleared unless the gates are closed and locked against road traffic
options.B: Two level crossings on the same road are operated by one gateman
options.C: The gates of the level crossing are provided with locks and keys
options.D: The level crossing is connected by telephone with the station

e: A level crossing is interlocked when its gates or barriers are interlocked with the signals, so that the signal for a train cannot be cleared unless the gates are closed and locked against road traffic.

q: Steel girders of a bridge are given a slight upward curve, known as camber, at the time of fabrication and erection in order to:

options.A: Improve the appearance of the bridge
options.B: Compensate for the deflection of the girder under load, so that the girder assumes the correct profile when loaded
options.C: Increase the waterway under the bridge
options.D: Reduce the weight of steel required in the girder

e: Steel girders are fabricated with camber - a slight upward curve - to compensate for the deflection of the girder under load, so that it assumes the correct profile when loaded.

q: The 'cut water' of a bridge pier is:

options.A: The arrangement made to drain water off the deck of the bridge
options.B: The deepest level up to which scour takes place at the pier
options.C: The channel cut in the river bed to divert the flow away from the pier
options.D: The pointed or rounded end of the pier facing the flow of water, shaped so as to cut through the current and reduce resistance and scour

e: The cut water is the pointed or rounded end of a bridge pier facing the flow, shaped to cut through the current smoothly and thereby reduce resistance and scour at the pier.

q: A 'submersible' bridge across a stream is one which:

options.A: Is designed to be overtopped by the flood water of the stream during high floods, its deck being kept at a low level
options.B: Is built entirely below the bed level of the stream
options.C: Carries the railway line through a tunnel under the stream
options.D: Can be dismantled and removed before the flood season

e: A submersible bridge is designed with its deck at a low level so that it is overtopped by the flood water of the stream during high floods, traffic being suspended for that period.

q: Weep holes are provided in the body of a retaining wall in order to:

options.A: Reduce the quantity of masonry in the wall
options.B: Drain out the water that accumulates behind the wall and thereby relieve the pressure on the wall
options.C: Provide footholds for the inspection of the wall
options.D: Ventilate the filling behind the wall

e: Weep holes in a retaining wall drain out the water that accumulates behind the wall, relieving the water pressure which would otherwise push against and endanger the wall.

q: A damp proof course is provided in the walls of a building at about plinth level in order to:

options.A: Strengthen the wall against lateral thrust
options.B: Prevent the moisture from the ground rising into the wall and the building above
options.C: Provide a level surface for laying the floor
options.D: Protect the wall against white ants

e: A damp proof course at about plinth level forms an impervious barrier in the wall, preventing moisture from the ground from rising into the wall and the building above by capillary action.

q: The 'grade' of ordinary Portland cement, such as 43 grade or 53 grade, denotes:

options.A: The fineness to which the cement is ground
options.B: The setting time of the cement in minutes
options.C: The proportion of clinker present in the cement
options.D: The minimum compressive strength, in newtons per square millimetre, which the cement attains at 28 days

e: The grade of ordinary Portland cement, such as 43 or 53 grade, denotes the minimum compressive strength in newtons per square millimetre that the cement attains at 28 days.

q: 'Bulking' of sand, which has to be allowed for when concrete is proportioned by volume, refers to:

options.A: The increase in the volume of sand when it contains moisture, as compared with its volume when dry
options.B: The decrease in the volume of sand on compaction
options.C: The proportion of silt present in the sand
options.D: The grading of the sand into different sizes

e: Bulking of sand is the increase in its volume when it contains moisture, compared with its dry volume; it must be allowed for when concrete is proportioned by volume.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. 'Bleeding' of concrete is the appearance of water on the surface of freshly placed concrete after it has been compacted.
2. 'Segregation' of concrete is the separation of the coarse aggregate from the mortar in fresh concrete.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: bleeding is the appearance of water on the surface of freshly placed and compacted concrete, and segregation is the separation of the coarse aggregate from the mortar in fresh concrete.

q: Stirrups, that is, lateral reinforcement, provided in a reinforced cement concrete beam serve primarily to:

options.A: Increase the compressive strength of the concrete
options.B: Resist the shear forces in the beam and hold the main reinforcement in position
options.C: Reduce the deflection of the beam
options.D: Protect the main reinforcement against corrosion

e: Stirrups (lateral reinforcement) in an RCC beam primarily resist the shear forces in the beam and also hold the main reinforcement bars in position.

q: Guard rails are provided in the track on important bridges in order to:

options.A: Strengthen the track against the impact of trains
options.B: Carry the track circuit current on the bridge
options.C: Prevent the entry of road vehicles on the bridge
options.D: Guide a derailed vehicle along the bridge and prevent it from falling off the bridge

e: Guard rails on important bridges guide a derailed vehicle along the bridge, preventing it from falling off the bridge while it runs out its momentum.

q: Where rails of two different sections have to be joined together in a track, the joint is made by using:

options.A: Compromise fish plates, which are specially shaped to fit the two different rail sections
options.B: Ordinary fish plates bent to suit the two sections
options.C: An insulated joint between the two rails
options.D: A welded joint in all cases

e: Rails of two different sections are joined using compromise fish plates, which are specially shaped on the two sides to fit the profiles of the two different rail sections.

q: Groynes, also called spurs, constructed in a river projecting from its bank, serve to:

options.A: Measure the discharge of the river at the site
options.B: Provide a foundation for the piers of a bridge
options.C: Deflect the current of the river away from the bank and protect the bank against erosion
options.D: Divide the flow of the river equally between two channels

e: Groynes or spurs project from the river bank into the stream and deflect the current away from the bank, protecting the bank against erosion.

q: The nominal size of machine-crushed stone ballast used in broad gauge track is about:

options.A: 25 millimetres
options.B: 50 millimetres
options.C: 65 millimetres
options.D: 80 millimetres

e: The nominal size of machine-crushed stone ballast used in broad gauge track is about 50 millimetres.

q: 'Ballast pockets' which develop in the formation of a track are objectionable because they:

options.A: Increase the speed of trains on the section
options.B: Reduce the cushion of ballast under the sleepers
options.C: Improve the drainage of the formation
options.D: Are depressions in the formation filled with ballast which retain water, soften the formation and make the track unstable

e: Ballast pockets are depressions in the formation filled with ballast which retain water, soften the formation and make the track unstable, so they are objectionable and must be corrected.

q: Gabions, used in protection and training works in connection with railway bridges and embankments, are:

options.A: Boxes or crates of wire mesh filled with stones or boulders
options.B: Concrete blocks cast in the shape of interlocking rings
options.C: Bags filled with cement and sand laid under water
options.D: Steel sheets driven into the river bed along the bank

e: Gabions are boxes or crates of wire mesh filled with stones or boulders, used in protection and training works for bridges and embankments as they are flexible and permeable.

q: An 'open web' girder used for a railway bridge is a girder in which:

options.A: The top flange is left open for inspection
options.B: The web is formed by a framework of diagonal and vertical members acting as a truss, instead of a solid plate
options.C: The girder is made of two rolled steel joists placed side by side
options.D: The bearings at both ends are of the expansion type

e: In an open web girder, the web is not a solid plate but a framework of diagonal and vertical members acting as a truss, making the girder lighter for long spans.

q: A bridge across a stream or a road is described as a 'skew' bridge when:

options.A: Its deck is built at a slope from one end to the other
options.B: Its girders are of unequal lengths
options.C: The axis of the bridge makes an angle other than a right angle with the direction of the stream or the road which it crosses
options.D: It is built on a curve of the railway line

e: A bridge is a skew bridge when its axis makes an angle other than a right angle with the direction of the stream or road it crosses.

q: An abutment of a bridge, as distinguished from a pier, is the support which:

options.A: Supports the end of the bridge span and also retains the earth filling of the approach embankment behind it
options.B: Is provided in the middle of the span of the bridge
options.C: Supports two adjacent spans of the bridge
options.D: Is always founded on wells, and never on piles

e: An abutment supports the end of the bridge span and also retains the earth filling of the approach embankment behind it; a pier, by contrast, supports spans in between without retaining earth.

q: A pile foundation is adopted for a bridge or other structure when:

options.A: The structure is of a temporary nature
options.B: Hard rock is available at a shallow depth below the surface
options.C: The foundation is to be laid in dry ground only
options.D: The strata near the surface are too weak to bear the load, and the load has to be transferred to deeper strata of adequate bearing capacity

e: A pile foundation is adopted when the strata near the surface are too weak to bear the load, so that the load has to be transferred through piles to deeper strata of adequate bearing capacity.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A cofferdam is a temporary enclosure built in water to exclude the water from the foundation area, so that the foundation work can be carried out in the dry.
2. A caisson is a hollow structure which is sunk into the ground or the river bed and forms a part of the permanent foundation of the structure.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: a cofferdam is a temporary enclosure excluding water so foundation work can be done in the dry, while a caisson is sunk into the ground or river bed and forms part of the permanent foundation.

q: A lintel provided in a building is:

options.A: A vertical member supporting the roof of the building
options.B: A beam laid over the top of a wall to carry the parapet
options.C: A horizontal member provided over an opening, such as a door or a window, to support the load of the construction above the opening
options.D: A course of stones laid at the plinth level of the building

e: A lintel is a horizontal member provided over an opening such as a door or window, to support the load of the construction above the opening and transfer it to the sides.

q: The weight of one metre length of a steel reinforcement bar is given by the formula d2/162 kilograms, where d is the diameter of the bar in millimetres. The weight of one metre length of a bar of 16 millimetres diameter is:

options.A: 0.62 kilogram
options.B: 0.89 kilogram
options.C: 1.58 kilograms
options.D: 2.47 kilograms

e: Weight per metre = d2/162 = 16 x 16 / 162 = 256/162 = 1.58 kilograms.

q: A track gradient expressed as '1 in 200' means that the track:

options.A: Is 200 metres in length
options.B: Carries 200 trains in a day
options.C: Has 200 sleepers in its length
options.D: Rises or falls by 1 unit for every 200 units of horizontal distance

e: A gradient of '1 in 200' means the track rises or falls by 1 unit vertically for every 200 units of horizontal distance travelled.

q: The Register of Assets and Repairs (RAR) maintained for engineering assets primarily helps in:

options.A: Recording the bills passed for payment to contractors
options.B: Recording the attendance of gang staff engaged on maintenance
options.C: Maintaining the list of works included in the Pink Book
options.D: Keeping an asset-wise record of assets and the expenditure incurred on their repairs and renewals, so that their condition and renewal needs can be watched

e: The Register of Assets and Repairs keeps an asset-wise record of engineering assets and the expenditure on their repairs and renewals, so condition, life and renewal needs can be watched under the Engineering Code.

q: Finance scrutiny of a detailed estimate, as distinct from scrutiny of an abstract estimate, is mainly concerned with:

options.A: Deciding whether the work should be included in the Works Programme at all
options.B: Fixing the agency which will execute the work
options.C: Examining only the total lump-sum cost of the proposal
options.D: Item-wise examination of quantities, rates, provisions and the correctness of the allocation of the expenditure

e: Finance scrutiny of a detailed estimate is item-wise: quantities, rates, provisions and allocation are examined in detail, unlike an abstract estimate where only the total cost and need for the work are broadly considered.

q: Expenditure sanctioned by an authority which was not competent to sanction it is treated as:

options.A: A deposit work
options.B: Unauthorised/unsanctioned expenditure, requiring regularisation by the competent authority
options.C: A work of urgent nature
options.D: Expenditure chargeable to Miscellaneous Works Advances in all cases

e: Expenditure incurred under sanction of an authority not competent to sanction it is unauthorised or unsanctioned expenditure and must be regularised by sanction of the competent authority.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Expenditure should not ordinarily be incurred merely in anticipation of sanction.
2. In a genuine emergency, such as restoration of through communication after an accident, expenditure may be incurred first and sanction obtained subsequently.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: expenditure should not ordinarily be incurred in anticipation of sanction, but in a genuine emergency such as restoring through communication after an accident, work may start first and sanction follow.

q: During execution of a sanctioned station building work, it is decided to shift the building to a new location and add a foot over-bridge which was not provided in the sanctioned estimate. This change in scope is in the nature of:

options.A: A book adjustment
options.B: A write-back of liability
options.C: A token variation in quantities
options.D: A material modification of the sanctioned work

e: Shifting the site and adding a foot over-bridge not in the sanctioned estimate changes the scope and character of the work, so it is a material modification needing sanction as per the Engineering Code, not a mere variation.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A material modification which takes the total cost of a work beyond the powers of the authority which sanctioned the original estimate requires the sanction of the authority competent for the revised total cost.
2. A material modification can always be sanctioned by the original sanctioning authority, whatever the resulting total cost.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct: if a material modification takes the total cost beyond the powers of the original sanctioning authority, sanction of the authority competent for the revised total cost is required.

q: The Completion Certificate issued by the Engineer-in-charge under a works contract differs from the Completion Report of a work in that the Completion Certificate:

options.A: Compares the actual cost of the work with the sanctioned estimate for the purpose of closing the estimate
options.B: Certifies that the contractor has completed the work in accordance with the contract, whereas the Completion Report deals with the final cost of the work against its sanctioned estimate
options.C: Is prepared by the Accounts office for closing the Contractor's Ledger
options.D: Sanctions the excess over the estimate of the work

e: The Completion Certificate under GCC certifies the contractor completed the work per the contract, while the Completion Report compares final actual cost with the sanctioned estimate to close the estimate.

q: Entries in the Liability Register are particularly useful at the time of framing the budget because they show:

options.A: The earnings expected from the works in progress
options.B: The names of contractors whose tenders are under consideration
options.C: The value of materials lying at the sites of works
options.D: The committed liabilities already incurred which will require provision of funds in the ensuing period

e: The Liability Register shows committed liabilities already incurred on works in progress, so budget framing can provide funds in the ensuing period to meet payments falling due against those commitments.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Works Register watches expenditure work-wise against the sanctioned estimate of each work.
2. The Contractor's Ledger watches payments, advances and recoveries contractor-wise.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: the Works Register watches expenditure work-wise against each sanctioned estimate, while the Contractor's Ledger watches payments, advances and recoveries contractor-wise.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Fixed Asset Register records the assets created by a Railway, asset-wise, with their cost and location.
2. The Block Account is the asset-wise register maintained by each division for watching repairs of assets.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct: the Fixed Asset Register records assets asset-wise with cost and location; the Block Account is the capital-at-charge record, not a divisional register for watching repairs.

q: In the two-packet system of tendering, the first packet (Packet-1) submitted by a tenderer ordinarily contains:

options.A: Only the financial offer of the tenderer
options.B: The earnest money, eligibility/technical documents and the technical offer, without the financial rates
options.C: The performance guarantee for the work
options.D: The final bill of a work executed earlier by him

e: In the two-packet system Packet-1 contains earnest money, eligibility and technical documents and the technical offer only; financial rates are kept in the sealed Packet-2, opened later for qualified bidders.

q: Negotiations with tenderers, as a matter of policy:

options.A: Must be held in every tender to bring down the rates
options.B: Are held with all tenderers in turn until the lowest rate is obtained
options.C: Are a routine step before the meeting of the Tender Committee
options.D: Are to be avoided as a rule and resorted to only exceptionally, when the rates received are considered unreasonably high

e: As per tender policy and GFR principles, negotiations are to be avoided as a rule and held only exceptionally, normally with L1, when rates received are considered unreasonably high.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A variation is a change in quantities or scope which remains within the general scope and character of the contract.
2. A vitiation occurs when the change is so extensive that the contract, as altered, is fundamentally different in character from the contract originally made.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: a variation stays within the general scope and character of the contract, while vitiation is a change so extensive that the altered contract is fundamentally different from the contract originally made.

q: Quantities of an item under a contract increase during execution, but the increase is within the deviation limits laid down in the contract and the nature of the work is unchanged. The excess quantity is:

options.A: Treated as vitiation of the contract
options.B: Paid for at the contract rate, the change being a variation within the contract
options.C: Paid for only after a fresh tender is invited
options.D: Not payable to the contractor in any case

e: Excess quantity within the deviation limits in GCC, with the nature of work unchanged, is a variation within the contract and is paid at the contract rate; it is neither vitiation nor a fresh tender.

q: Price variation under a works contract is NOT admissible in respect of:

options.A: The labour component of the work executed by the contractor
options.B: The material component representing the contractor's own materials
options.C: Work done during the original stipulated period of completion
options.D: Departmental materials supplied by the Railways to the contractor at fixed issue rates given in the contract

e: Price variation is not admissible on departmental materials supplied by Railways at fixed issue rates in the contract, since the contractor bears no price risk on materials he does not purchase.

q: In the two-packet system, the financial packets of tenderers whose technical bids are found unacceptable are:

options.A: Opened and their rates recorded for future reference
options.B: Opened only if their earnest money is forfeited
options.C: Considered after negotiation with those tenderers
options.D: Returned to them unopened

e: In the two-packet system, financial packets of tenderers whose technical bids are unacceptable are returned unopened, so their rates are never disclosed or considered.

q: Conciliation of a contractual dispute, as distinguished from arbitration, is a process in which:

options.A: The conciliator passes a binding award enforceable as a decree
options.B: A settlement is attempted with the help of a conciliator, and a settlement becomes binding only when the parties agree to and sign it
options.C: The dispute is decided by the Engineer as an excepted matter
options.D: The Tender Committee reconsiders its recommendation

e: In conciliation a settlement is binding only when the parties agree and sign it; unlike arbitration, the conciliator passes no binding award enforceable as a decree.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Performance Guarantee is furnished to secure the due performance of the contract by the contractor.
2. The Security Deposit can never be utilised for recovering amounts due from the contractor to the Railways.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct: Performance Guarantee secures due performance of the contract; Security Deposit can be utilised for recovering amounts due from the contractor, so statement 2 is false.

q: A Letter of Credit in contract transactions is generally used in connection with:

options.A: Works executed departmentally by the Railway's own staff
options.B: Purchases, particularly import contracts, where payment is made by the bank to the supplier against fulfilment of the conditions and documents specified in the credit
options.C: Payment of on-account running bills of works contractors
options.D: Refund of security deposit to contractors

e: A Letter of Credit is used mainly for purchases, particularly imports, where the bank pays the supplier against the documents and conditions specified in the credit.

q: BOOT differs from BOT mainly in that, under BOOT, during the concession period the asset is:

options.A: Owned by the private partner, and is transferred to the authority at the end of the period
options.B: Owned by the authority from the very beginning in all respects
options.C: Owned jointly by all the tenderers
options.D: Not operated by the private partner at all

e: Under BOOT (Build, Own, Operate, Transfer) the private partner owns the asset during the concession period and transfers it to the authority at the end; under BOT ownership does not vest in the partner in the same way.

q: In a toll-based BOT concession, the traffic/revenue risk is borne primarily by:

options.A: The concessionaire, who recovers his investment from the toll/user charges collected
options.B: The authority, which pays a fixed annuity irrespective of traffic
options.C: The contractor's bank alone
options.D: The users of the facility through departmental charges

e: In a toll-based BOT the concessionaire bears traffic and revenue risk because he recovers investment from toll or user charges actually collected; in an annuity model the authority pays fixed annuity instead.

q: Payment under a GCC for Services contract for housekeeping of a station is ordinarily made:

options.A: On the basis of measurements recorded in the Measurement Book
options.B: As a lump sum before the services commence
options.C: Only after the expiry of five years of service
options.D: Periodically, for the services actually rendered during the period, as verified from attendance/output records

e: Under GCC for Services, payment is made periodically for services actually rendered during the period, as verified from attendance and output records, not on Measurement Book measurements or as advance lump sum.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Foreclosure (short-closure) of a contract is ordered when the remaining work is no longer required, and not on account of the contractor's default.
2. Determination of a contract is ordered on account of the contractor's default and the balance work may be got done at his risk and cost.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: foreclosure is short-closure when the remaining work is no longer required and not for contractor default, while determination is for contractor default and balance work may be done at his risk and cost.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. An officer exercising delegated financial powers cannot sub-delegate those powers to a subordinate unless the delegation itself expressly permits sub-delegation.
2. An officer may sub-delegate his financial powers at his discretion even where the Schedule of Powers is silent on the point.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct: delegated financial powers cannot be sub-delegated unless the delegation or Schedule of Powers expressly permits it; silence in the SOP does not give discretion to sub-delegate.

q: The correct sequence of surveys/investigations for a proposed new railway line is:

options.A: Final Location Survey, Reconnaissance Survey, PETS
options.B: Reconnaissance Survey, Preliminary Engineering-cum-Traffic Survey (PETS), Final Location Survey
options.C: PETS, Final Location Survey, Reconnaissance Survey
options.D: Reconnaissance Survey, Final Location Survey, PETS

e: The correct sequence is Reconnaissance Survey, then Preliminary Engineering-cum-Traffic Survey (PETS), then Final Location Survey, as investigations progress from broad corridor selection to final alignment.

q: Provision of limited height subways at a number of level crossings in a section, sanctioned together as a single work for allotment and execution, is an example of:

options.A: A deposit work
options.B: A material modification
options.C: A work charged to Miscellaneous Works Advances
options.D: An umbrella work

e: Several similar small works, here limited height subways at many level crossings, sanctioned together as one work for allotment and execution form an umbrella work.

q: At the completion of a work, a provision made for a liability is found to be more than the amount actually payable, and the excess provision is credited back to the work. This adjustment is called:

options.A: Write-off
options.B: Write-back
options.C: Re-appropriation
options.D: Vitiation

e: Crediting back to the work the excess of a provision for liability over the amount actually payable is a write-back of liability; it is distinct from a write-off of an irrecoverable amount.

q: An advance paid in connection with a work is established, after due enquiry, to be irrecoverable. With the sanction of the competent authority, the amount is removed from the books by:

options.A: Write-back
options.B: Transfer to the Material-at-Site account
options.C: Write-off
options.D: Adjustment against the earnest money of other tenderers

e: An advance established after enquiry as irrecoverable is removed from the books by write-off with the sanction of the competent authority; write-back applies to excess liability provisions, not irrecoverable advances.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A lease of railway land creates a leasehold interest in the land in favour of the lessee for the term of the lease.
2. A licence of railway land is a mere permission to use the land and creates no interest in the land in favour of the licensee.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: a lease creates a leasehold interest in the land for the lease term, while a licence is mere permission to use the land and creates no interest in the land for the licensee.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Departmental charges are recovered where the Railway itself executes a work for an outside body.
2. Supervision charges are recovered where the outside body executes the work itself and the Railway only supervises it.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: departmental charges are recovered when Railways execute a work for an outside body, while supervision charges are recovered when the outside body executes it itself and Railways only supervise.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. An urgency certificate is meant only for a bona fide emergency and must record the nature of the urgency.
2. An urgency certificate may be issued as a routine measure whenever calling tenders is likely to take time.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct: an urgency certificate is only for a bona fide emergency and must record the nature of urgency; it cannot be used routinely merely because tendering takes time.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Where even quotations are dispensed with for a work, the reasons for doing so must be recorded and the sanction of the competent authority obtained.
2. Dispensing with quotations requires neither recorded reasons nor any sanction.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct: dispensing even with quotations requires recorded reasons and sanction of the competent authority; it is not a sanction-free, unrecorded course.

q: The Standard Measurement Book is useful for periodical repair services of buildings because:

options.A: It records the measurements of all new works of the division
options.B: It contains the comparative statement of tenders for repairs
options.C: It is a register of the assets created during the year
options.D: It records the standard measurements of repetitive items once, so that bills for recurring services at prescribed intervals can be passed without fresh measurement on every occasion

e: The Standard Measurement Book records standard measurements of repetitive building repair items once, so bills for recurring services at prescribed intervals can be passed without fresh measurement each time.

q: A standard of propriety to be observed in entering into contracts on behalf of the Railways is that:

options.A: The contract should invariably be given to the contractor already working in the section
options.B: The liability of the Railways under the contract may be left uncertain if the work is urgent
options.C: The terms of the contract should be settled only after the work is completed
options.D: A contract should not be entered into which involves an uncertain or indefinite liability for the Railways

e: A standard of financial propriety in contracts, also in GFR, is that no contract should be entered into involving an uncertain or indefinite liability for the Railways; terms must be definite before commitment.

q: A contractor abandons a work midway and the contract is determined. The balance work is completed through another agency at a cost higher than the contract rates. The extra cost so incurred is:

options.A: Borne by the Railways as a normal cost of the work
options.B: Recoverable from the defaulting contractor, as the work was completed at his risk and cost
options.C: Recovered from the tenderers who did not take up the work
options.D: Adjusted against the departmental charges of the work

e: On determination for abandonment, balance work completed through another agency at higher cost is done at the risk and cost of the defaulting contractor, and the extra cost is recoverable from him under GCC.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under the Hybrid Annuity Model, a part of the project cost is paid by the authority during the construction period itself.
2. Under the pure annuity model, the private partner's recovery is wholly through annuity payments after construction, with no part of the project cost paid during construction.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: under Hybrid Annuity Model part of project cost is paid by the authority during construction, while under pure annuity recovery is wholly through annuity payments after construction.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. An engineering survey of a proposed line primarily estimates the traffic likely to be carried and the earnings expected from it.
2. A traffic survey of a proposed line primarily assesses the traffic prospects and the remunerativeness of the proposal.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 2 is correct: a traffic survey assesses traffic prospects and remunerativeness; an engineering survey deals with alignment and engineering feasibility and cost, not primarily earnings estimation.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A joint venture is an association of firms which jointly undertakes a work, its members being jointly and severally liable to the Railways.
2. A Special Purpose Vehicle is a separate company or entity created specifically for executing a particular project.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: joint venture members are jointly and severally liable to Railways, while a Special Purpose Vehicle is a separate entity created specifically for executing a particular project.

q: Extension of the currency of a services contract beyond its original term:

options.A: Takes place automatically if the contractor continues to provide the service
options.B: Requires the sanction of the competent authority and is considered on the basis of the satisfactory performance of the contractor
options.C: Can be ordered by the contractor by giving a notice to the Railways
options.D: Does not require any sanction if the rates remain unchanged

e: Extension of currency of a services contract requires sanction of the competent authority and is considered on satisfactory performance of the contractor; it is never automatic or at the contractor's notice.

q: Finance returns a detailed estimate pointing out errors in rates and allocation and asking for their correction before it agrees to the proposal. At this stage, Finance has:

options.A: Accorded its concurrence to the estimate
options.B: Vetted the estimate, concurrence being accorded only after the observations are complied with
options.C: Accorded administrative approval to the work
options.D: Sanctioned the excess over the estimate

e: When Finance returns an estimate with observations on rates and allocation for correction, it has only vetted it; concurrence is accorded only after the observations are complied with.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Material-at-Site account is debited with the value of materials issued for a work.
2. If the Material-at-Site account is not cleared of unconsumed materials on completion, the cost of the work remains overstated to that extent.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: Material-at-Site account is debited with materials issued for a work, and if unconsumed materials are not cleared on completion, the cost of the work stays overstated to that extent.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. As far as practicable, a revised estimate should be got sanctioned before expenditure in excess of the sanctioned estimate is incurred.
2. Excess over a sanctioned estimate is automatically permissible so long as funds are available in the grant for the work.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct: a revised estimate should as far as practicable be sanctioned before excess expenditure is incurred; availability of funds in the grant does not by itself permit excess over estimate.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Engineering Code contains the rules relating to estimates, tenders and contracts for engineering works.
2. The Works Manual contains the classification of stores items and the procedure for their purchase.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct: the Engineering Code covers estimates, tenders and contracts for engineering works; classification and purchase of stores is dealt with in the Stores Code, not the Works Manual.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A feasibility study/PETS examination of a major project precedes the preparation of its Detailed Project Report.
2. Investment approval of a major project is obtained on the basis of the Detailed Project Report.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: feasibility study or PETS precedes the Detailed Project Report of a major project, and investment approval is obtained on the basis of the Detailed Project Report.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Railway land given on long-term lease for commercial development creates a leasehold interest in favour of the developer for the lease term.
2. Railway land licensed temporarily, for example for cultivation or as way-leave, also creates a leasehold interest in favour of the licensee.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct: long-term lease for commercial development creates a leasehold interest for the term; temporary licence, for example for cultivation or way-leave, creates no such interest.

q: Works expenditure which is 'charged' on the Consolidated Fund of India is expenditure which:

options.A: Is not submitted to the vote of Parliament, though it may be discussed by Parliament
options.B: Is met entirely from the earnings of the Railways
options.C: Is sanctioned personally by the General Manager of a Zonal Railway
options.D: Is incurred only on works of an urgent nature

e: Charged expenditure is charged on the Consolidated Fund of India: it is not submitted to the vote of Parliament, though Parliament may discuss it.

q: Voted expenditure on railway works is expenditure which:

options.A: Is charged on the Contingency Fund of India
options.B: Requires no provision in the Demands for Grants
options.C: Is met from the deposits made by outside bodies for deposit works
options.D: Is submitted to and voted by Parliament through the Demands for Grants

e: Voted expenditure is submitted to and voted by Parliament through the Demands for Grants, unlike charged expenditure which is not put to vote.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Charged expenditure is not put to the vote of Parliament.
2. Voted expenditure also cannot be discussed by Parliament before it is voted.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct: charged expenditure is not put to the vote of Parliament; voted expenditure is fully discussed by Parliament before voting, so statement 2 is false.

q: A completion estimate of a work differs from its completion report in that the completion estimate:

options.A: Is prepared before the detailed estimate of the work is sanctioned
options.B: Records the measurements of the work done by the contractor
options.C: Is prepared when the work is nearing completion to arrive at its anticipated final cost, whereas the completion report is drawn up after completion comparing the actual cost with the sanctioned estimate
options.D: Is prepared by the contractor and submitted along with his final bill

e: A completion estimate is prepared when the work is nearing completion to arrive at anticipated final cost, while the completion report is drawn after completion comparing actual cost with the sanctioned estimate.

q: Where the final cost of a completed work exceeds its sanctioned estimate, the completion report of the work must:

options.A: Simply record the excess without any explanation, the excess being automatically regularised
options.B: Be withheld until the contractor agrees to bear the excess cost
options.C: Recover the excess from the departmental charges of the work
options.D: Explain the reasons for the excess, and the excess is regularised with the sanction of the authority competent to sanction the total final cost of the work

e: Where final cost exceeds the sanctioned estimate, the completion report must explain reasons for the excess, and the excess is regularised by sanction of the authority competent for the total final cost.
